question.problem:
The point $P$ with coordinates $(-15,6)$ lies on the curve $y=f(\frac{1}{3}x).$ Find the point $Q$ that must lie on $y=f(x).$

The coordinates of $Q$ are $(${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$).$
question.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)=f(3\cdot (\frac{1}{3}x)),$ the function $y=f(x)$ represents a compression of the function $y=f(\frac{1}{3}x)$ by a factor of $3$ parallel to the $x$-axis. This has the effect of dividing the $x$-coordinates of all points on $y=f(\frac{1}{3}x)$ by $3.$

Therefore, the point $(-15,6)$ on $f(\frac{1}{3}x)$ is mapped to the point $(\frac{-15}{3},6)=(-5,6),$ and this point must lie on the graph of $y=f(x).$
